req_desc:
Run manifest and health check
/app/run.json installs, builds and serves the app on the public port, and the health path answers ok while storage or the directory is down, as set out in Deployment.

Credentials from the environment
Every service URL and credential is read from the environment at start and is never hard-coded, logged or sent to the browser.

Schema and seed on every start
Each start applies the database schema, the bucket and the directory collection fields idempotently, and seeds an empty database exactly once with the records in Seed data.

Same-origin server boundary
The server enforces the body limits, content types, origin check, response headers and never-served paths in Server boundary.

Server clock in Phoenix time
The server publishes its clock and the company date in America/Phoenix and judges every expiry on that clock, and the clock-control instance can move it, as qualified in Business rules.

One error shape and order
Every error response uses the single JSON error shape and the check order stated at the top of API.

Drafting-table layout
At desktop width the signed-in screen has three panes separated by hairline rules with no shadows: a rail with the tree and meter, a path bar over the list, and a details panel with activity.

Blueprint palette and Plex type
The screen uses the warm paper ground, dark ink, one blueprint-blue accent, rust for warnings and the IBM Plex faces, sets every numeral in tabular mono, and meets WCAG 2.2 AA contrast.

Three viewports without sideways scroll
At 375x812, 768x1024 and 1280x800 every screen fits the viewport width with the pane arrangement given in Screens and layout.

Homing flight
After a move is acknowledged, name chips fly on a curved path from the moved rows to the destination with the timing, stagger, cap and count steps given in Motion and effects.

Reduced-motion homing
Under reduced motion no chip flies and nothing animates: moved rows leave at once and the destination shows a static plus badge until focus next moves.

One polite announcements region
Selection counts, move results, upload results and every other async result are announced once each, through the single polite status region, with the exact copy in Feedback states.

Live updates on every open screen
Every state change reaches every open screen allowed to see it within the delays in Business rules, updating lists, tree counts, activity and the meter without a reload.

Honest storage and time wiring
File bytes live only in object storage and people only in the directory, no browser code decides whether a grant, bin item, handover, link or upload has expired, and storage and directory health are re-probed on a timer so recovery needs no restart.

Sign in through the people directory
Email and password are checked against the directory, a server-side session cookie is set, and wrong credentials get the rejection in API.

Staff and partner capabilities
Each action is allowed only to the people listed for it in Business rules, and every other caller is refused with the status stated there.

People picker search
The share and handover pickers search the directory as the person types, work by keyboard as a combobox, and show each person's name, firm and kind.

Directory outage
While the directory is unreachable, sign-in and the pickers show the directory outage copy and the service status reads down, while existing sessions, access checks and grant changes keep working.

Folder tree with item counts
The rail tree shows every folder the person can see, each with a mono count of the live files directly inside it, always matching the API.

File list with sort, view and search
The centre shows the open folder as a list or a grid in any of the six sort orders, and search finds files by name across everything the person can see.

State kept in the address
The open folder, view, sort and search live in the address, so Back, reload and a copied address in a second tab show the same state.

Recent files
Recent lists the 50 most recently active live files the person can see, each with its current folder, and drops files that are binned or purged.

Keyboard folder tree and file list
The tree and list follow the key map in Interactions, including expand, collapse, typeahead, extending and toggling selection, cut, paste and Enter.

Details panel and activity ledger
The details panel shows the selected item's facts, its preview and its activity from the ledger, newest first, with mono Phoenix times.

Browse a project journey
A project engineer signs in, opens a project folder from the tree, switches to grid, sorts newest first, searches, opens a file's details, and gets the same state back after a reload.

Resumable multipart upload
Uploads run through server-tracked multipart sessions in fixed-size parts, and a paused upload resumes after a page reload from its last confirmed part.

Storage confirms every upload
A file's row, list entry, activity and bytes on the meter appear only after storage confirms the completed object, and cancelled or abandoned uploads leave no row and no object.

Pause, resume and cancel
Upload sessions follow the state machine in Business rules, and each illegal step gets its exact rejection.

Abandoned uploads expire
An upload left paused or idle for the configured period (24 hours by default) becomes expired on the server, and its parts are removed.

Storage meter
Staff see a company storage meter equal to the sum of confirmed object sizes, bin included, which changes only when an upload completes or a file is purged.

Upload journey
A project engineer uploads a multi-part file into a folder, pauses it, reloads, resumes, and sees the file land in the list, the folder count, the meter and the announcement together.

Uploads refused during a storage outage
While object storage is unreachable, the outage banner shows, the service status reads down, and starting an upload is refused with the storage outage copy while nothing is created.

Previews during a storage outage
While object storage is unreachable, previews and content links show the storage outage state while lists, details and activity keep working.

Move files with replay safety
A move takes a selection and a destination, moves the free files, reports locked and lost files, and returns the stored result when an idempotency key is repeated.

One winner for concurrent moves
When several people move the same file at once exactly one move wins, and every loser's response and screen show the winning folder.

Counts, ledger and meter move together
Each action changes folder counts, the activity ledger and the storage figures in one step, never one without the others.

Move to dialog
The Move to dialog offers a destination tree that works by keyboard, keeps Tab inside the dialog, closes on Escape and returns focus to its opener.

Cut, paste and drag journey
A project engineer moves a mixed selection by Ctrl X and Ctrl V, by dragging onto a tree node and by Move to, and a second open screen sees the same result.

Lock and unlock issued files
Document controllers lock and unlock files, and a locked file shows its lock badge on every open screen within the push delay.

Locked files stay put
Locked files are never moved, renamed or binned, and mixed selections act on the free files and report how many stayed.

Issue a set journey
A document controller locks an issued set, then an engineer moves it together with free files and sees the free files fly while the locked rows show Stayed.

Timed partner grants
Project owners and document controllers give outside partners viewer or editor access to a folder or file until an end date in the company zone, and can change or remove it.

Default grant length
A new grant made without an end date gets the default length in force on the day it is made.

Shared with me
A partner sees only granted items, each with its role, Phoenix end date and server-given days left, and every other id answers not found.

Share dialog journey
A project engineer opens Share on a folder, picks a partner by keyboard, sets editor access until a date, and sees the grant listed with its end date.

Grants end at Phoenix midnight
A grant gives access through the whole of its end date in Phoenix and gives nothing from the next Phoenix midnight, whatever the partner's own zone or device clock.

Fallback to inherited access
When a timed editor grant ends, the partner keeps only what other active grants on parent folders give, or nothing, and never a leftover role.

Ended access refused everywhere
After a grant ends, every route for that item refuses the partner as not found, including content links issued earlier.

Access-ended notice
When a grant ends, the partner's open screen removes the items, closes their preview and shows the in-app notice within the expiry delay in Business rules, with no email.

Downgrade and removal on next request
A partner lowered from editor to viewer, or removed, is refused on their very next write or read, mid-session.

Edit actions drop live
The partner's open screen loses its edit actions or items as soon as the change is pushed, and shows the notice in Feedback states.

Bin with days left
Staff bin free files, and each binned row shows its original folder, binned date, server-given days left and the retention rule that applies.

Restore and delete forever
Staff restore binned files to their folder, and document controllers delete them forever, which removes the object and lowers the meter on every screen.

Scheduled purge
A binned file is purged for good at the start of its purge date in Phoenix, which removes its object and lowers the meter live, as qualified in Business rules.

Effective-dated policies
The office administrator schedules bin retention and default grant length from a future date, earlier items keep the rule in force when they were binned or granted, and a scheduled change can be withdrawn before it starts.

Policy settings journey
The office administrator schedules a shorter bin retention and sees it in the schedule, and once it applies the bin shows the old and new rules side by side.

Handover offers
Project owners and document controllers offer a project folder to another staff member, who accepts or declines it, and each illegal step gets its exact rejection.

Handover lapse
An offer not accepted by the end of its Phoenix lapse date lapses on the server, ownership stays with the giver, and the giver is told in the app.

Handover journey
A project engineer offers a project to a colleague, the colleague accepts it from Handovers, and both screens show the new owner.

Phone layout and touch selection
At 375 px wide the rail opens as a drawer, a long press starts a selection, the action bar's targets are at least 44 px, and the homing flight aims at the path bar.
/app/run.json exists with string install, build, serve and "_schema":"run-manifest-v1", and nothing else is needed to start the app.

THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md at /app lists every shipped package with its version and licence, plus the IBM Plex fonts and the Lucide icons; shipped packages means the production dependency tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json.
Every shipped package (same definition) and bundled asset is under MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD or OFL-1.1.
The only datastores are PostgreSQL, MinIO and PocketBase; there is no SQLite, Redis, in-memory store treated as the record, or state kept in files on disk.
The browser loads no script, font, style or icon from any origin other than the app's own.
The provided service definitions and dev credentials are left unchanged.
Application source for the server and the browser is written in TypeScript.
